question: Why does the ionization energy of a hydrogen-like atom increase with the atomic number $Z$?

options.A: Higher Z means more neutrons, which stabilize the electron.
options.B: Higher Z increases the positive charge of the nucleus, binding the electron more tightly.
options.C: Higher Z increases the radius of the orbit, making it harder to remove the electron.
options.D: Higher Z reduces the mass of the electron.
